guard: an omitted read set means NO channels, at the loader, at the mint, and at the send
why: THE DEFAULT WAS IN FOUR PLACES AND THE SUITE HAD TO SEE ALL OF THEM, which is why there are
three mutations here and not one. The loader, the provisioner/mint and the endpoint each wrote
`["general"]` independently, and each one alone is enough to put a DM-only seat on a channel
nobody named. A guard that watched only the loader would have gone green on a tree where the
mint still baked the channel row into every credential.
THE CREDENTIAL MUTATION IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS, because its regression is SILENT in every
surface an operator looks at. Restore the mint default and the persona still says nothing about
channels, the roster looks the same, and the only difference is a `chat.*.*.general` row in the
cred that the broker will honour. The suite catches it by asking the BROKER (a native subscribe
under those creds), not by reading the JWT: a mint that lists no row and a server that refuses
the subscribe are different claims, and only the second one is the boundary.
THE LOADER CELL IS AIMED AT A THROW, and that shaped the test rather than the fixture. Under the
old default a persona with `allowSubscribe: [ops]` and no `subscribe` was REJECTED at load: the
invented `general` read set was not within its own ACL. A bare `loadAgentFile` would abort the
suite before the cell named itself, and an unattributed crash grades as WRONG-RED, so the load is
wrapped and the cell reports. The regression direction is the point: this file was always
coherent and the default is what rejected it.
THE SEND MUTATION RESTORES A FALLBACK, NOT AN ERROR, which is the shape worth naming. With
`?? "general"` back in place nothing throws and nothing crashes: the endpoint publishes to a
channel the caller never chose, and for a scoped agent that publish is denied by the broker
fire-and-forget, so the caller sees success. The cell is a refusal assertion for exactly that
reason, since there is no exception to catch and no error to read.
TWO CELLS WERE FIXED ON THE TEST SIDE BEFORE THIS SET WAS TRUSTED, neither of which any
mutation would have caught, because both were about a cell that could pass while measuring
nothing. "It does not fall back to general" read the refusal text for the absence of a word,
and the helper answers an EMPTY STRING when the call did not reject at all, which satisfies
"does not mention general" trivially. That cell was loudest in exactly the state it exists to
catch. And "a no-channel send resolves to that channel" asserted only that nothing threw, which
is equally true of a send that quietly resolved somewhere else, so it now reads the destination
off the returned message and names it. A mutation set grades the code; it cannot tell you a cell
was vacuous, because a vacuous cell reddens on cue for the wrong reason.
NOT GRADED HERE, and named rather than implied: the connector's own env-level resolution
(`configFromEnv`) has the same tail default and lives in another package, so it is graded by
`pnpm smoke:session-channels` against that package's source. And the MANAGER's copy of the
default (`implementations/manager/src/manager.ts`, `?? subscribe ?? []` in the detached-spawn
door) is graded by `pnpm smoke:events-grant` (cell 4b, mutation G8): a fixture here could reach
neither, since this suite imports core by relative specifier and loads no other package.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY, checked rather than assumed: the suite imports `../src/index.js`, so the
bytes mutated are the bytes executed. There is no `dist` in the path and no build in the
command. A `bin/smoke/` home would have resolved `@cotal-ai/core` to its build and graded a
stale copy of exactly the four lines this change edits.

mutations.name: the agent-file loader defaults an omitted read set back to general
mutations.expectRed: a persona with a read ACL and no subscribe loads (an omitted read set is empty, not general)
mutations.cell: a persona with a read ACL and no subscribe loads (an omitted read set is empty, not general)
mutations.note: The shipped state before this change. It is not a silent regression at the loader, it is a LOUD one in the wrong direction: a persona scoped to `ops` and naming no boot channel is rejected for reading `general`, a channel it never wrote down. Every other consequence of the old default is silent, so this is the one place the behaviour argues with itself in the operator's face.

mutations.name: the mint defaults an omitted read ACL back to general, so every channel-less agent carries the row
mutations.expectRed: a persona with no read set mints NO channel read row: the broker denies chat.*.*.general
mutations.cell: a persona with no read set mints NO channel read row: the broker denies chat.*.*.general
mutations.note: The security half, and the silent one. Nothing in the persona, the roster or the logs changes; only the credential does, and it now authorizes a channel read the agent never asked for. Graded at the broker rather than at the mint, so the cell is about what nats-server will actually honour.

mutations.name: the endpoint restores the general fallback, so a channel-less send publishes instead of refusing
mutations.expectRed: multicast with no channel and no subscription REFUSES
mutations.cell: multicast with no channel and no subscription REFUSES
mutations.note: A fallback, not a crash, which is why it needs its own cell: the `channel === undefined` branch below simply goes dead, nothing throws, and the caller is told the send succeeded while the broker drops it. The same mutation also reddens the two cells that read the refusal text, and the leave-your-last-channel cell that depends on it; naming one is enough, and naming the first one keeps the verdict about the send rather than about leave.
